arxiv-1511-07041.title: SceneNet: Understanding Real World Indoor Scenes With Synthetic Data
arxiv-1511-07041.creator: Ankur Handa, Viorica Pătrăucean, Vijay Badrinarayanan, Simon Stent and, Roberto Cipolla
arxiv-1511-07041.description: Abstract Scene understanding is a prerequisite to many high level tasks for any automated intelligent machine operating in real world environments. Recent attempts with supervised learning have shown promise in this direction but also highlighted the need for enormous quantity of supervised data — performance increases in proportion to the amount of data used.

arxiv-2102-09002.title: Impartial selection with prior information
arxiv-2102-09002.creator: Ioannis Caragiannis, George Christodoulou, Nicos Protopapas
arxiv-2102-09002.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ioannis Caragiannis, George Christodoulou, Nicos Protopapas. We study the problem of impartial selection , a topic that lies at the intersection of computational social choice and mechanism design. The goal is to select the most popular individual among a set of community members. The input can be modeled as a directed graph, where each node represents an individual, and a directed edge indicates nomination or approval of a community member to another.

arxiv-2103-04329.title: Pose Discrepancy Spatial Transformer Based Feature Disentangling for Partial Aspect Angles SAR Target Recognition
arxiv-2103-04329.creator: Zaidao Wen, Member, IEEE, Jiaxiang Liu, Zhunga Liu, Member, IEEE, Quan Pan, Member, IEEE
arxiv-2103-04329.description: Abstract This letter presents a novel framework termed DistSTN for the task of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) automatic target recognition (ATR). In contrast to the conventional SAR ATR algorithms, DistSTN considers a more challenging practical scenario for non-cooperative targets whose aspect angles for training are incomplete and limited in a partial range while those of testing samples are unlimited.

arxiv-2109-00150.title: Federated Reconnaissance: Efficient, Distributed, Class-Incremental Learning
arxiv-2109-00150.creator: Sean M. Hendryx, Dharma Raj KC, Bradley Walls, Clayton T. Morrison
arxiv-2109-00150.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sean M. Hendryx, Dharma Raj KC, Bradley Walls, Clayton T. Morrison. We describe federated reconnaissance, a class of learning problems in which distributed clients learn new concepts independently and communicate that knowledge efficiently. In particular, we propose an evaluation framework and methodological baseline for a system in which each client is expected to learn a growing set of classes and communicate knowledge of those classes efficiently with other clients, such that, after knowledge merging, the clients should be able to accurately discriminate between classes

arxiv-2112-07667.title: The Sensitivity of Eclipse Mapping to Planetary Rotation Journal: AAS Journals Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ) , Colorcet ( Kovesi 2015 ) , python-colormath ( Taylor 2018 ) , Jupyter ( Kluyver et al. 2016 ) , Matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) , Numpy ( van der Walt et al. 2011 ) , Scikit-lear
arxiv-2112-07667.creator: Arthur D. Adams, Emily Rauscher
arxiv-2112-07667.description: Abstract Mapping exoplanets across phases and during secondary eclipse is a powerful technique for characterizing Hot Jupiters in emission. Since these planets are expected to rotate about axes normal to their orbital planes, with rotation periods synchronized with their orbital periods, mapping provides a direct correspondence between orbital phase and planetary longitude.

arxiv-2402-19002.title: GoalNet: Goal Areas Oriented Pedestrian Trajectory Prediction
arxiv-2402-19002.creator: Ching-Lin Lee, Zhi-Xuan Wang, Kuan-Ting Lai, Amar Fadillah
arxiv-2402-19002.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ching-Lin Lee, Zhi-Xuan Wang, Kuan-Ting Lai, Amar Fadillah. Predicting the future trajectories of pedestrians on the road is an important task for autonomous driving. The pedestrian trajectory prediction is affected by scene paths, pedestrian’s intentions and decision-making, which is a multi-modal problem. Most recent studies use past trajectories to predict a variety of potential future trajectory distributions, which do not account for the scene context and pedestrian targets.

arxiv-2408-12874.title: Enumeration of dihypergraphs with specified degrees and edge types
arxiv-2408-12874.creator: Catherine Greenhill, Tamás Makai
arxiv-2408-12874.description: Abstract A directed hypergraph (dihypergraph) consists of a set of vertices and a set of hyperarcs, where each hyperarc is partitioned into a head and a tail. Directed hypergraphs are useful in many applications, including the study of chemical reactions or relational databases.

arxiv-2509-17129.title: Decaying vector dark matter with low reheating temperature for KM3NeT signal and its impact on gravitational waves
arxiv-2509-17129.creator: Sarif Khan, Jongkuk Kim, Hyun Min Lee
arxiv-2509-17129.description: Abstract We propose a new model to explain the KM3NeT neutrino event through a low reheating scenario with a suppression in the GW spectrum originating from cosmic string networks. To achieve this, we extend the SM gauge sector by an abelian gauge symmetry and a singlet scalar.

arxiv-2510-22563.title: Diffusion operators on p p -adic analytic manifolds
arxiv-2510-22563.creator: Patrick Erik Bradley
arxiv-2510-22563.description: Abstract Kernel functions for Laplacian integral operators are constructed on p p -adic analytic manifolds using charts and transition maps like in Riemannian geometry. In the compact case, an operator of Vladimirov-Taibleson type parametrised by a real parameter s s is defined.

pmc-11505209.title: Community-associated Carbapenem-Resistant Organism Case Investigations in New York City, December 2020-May 2023
pmc-11505209.creator: Celina Santiago, Ying Lin, Ulrike Siemetzki-Kapoor, Nicole Burton, Katelynn Devinney, Balan Dominique, Portier Thomas, William Greendyke, Molly Kratz, Catharine Prussing, Kailee Cummings, Rebecca Zimba, Karen Alroy
pmc-11505209.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Epidemiology of carbapenem-resistant organisms (CRO) has focused on transmission in acute care hospital or long-term care facility (LTCF) settings. Few investigations have examined community-associated (CA)-CRO, with no consensus about common exposures. To explore possible exposures, the New York City (NYC) Department of Health and Mental Hygiene investigated suspected CA-CRO cases through routine surveillance among NYC residents with specimens collected during December 2020-May 2023.

pmc-11506918.title: Evaluation of Ability of Inactivated Biomasses of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus and Saccharomyces cerevisiae to Adsorb Aflatoxin B1 In Vitro
pmc-11506918.creator: Rogério Cury Pires, Julia da Costa Calumby, Roice Eliana Rosim, Rogério D’Antonio Pires, Aline Moreira Borowsky, Sher Ali, Esther Lima de Paiva, Ramon Silva, Tatiana Colombo Pimentel, Adriano Gomes da Cruz, Carlos Augusto Fernandes de Oliveira, Carlos Humberto Corassin, Mahmoud Yolmeh
pmc-11506918.description: Biological decontamination strategies using microorganisms to adsorb aflatoxins have shown promising results for reducing the dietary exposure to these contaminants. In this study, the ability of inactivated biomasses of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus (LRB) and Saccharomyces cerevisiae (SCB) incorporated alone or in combination into functional yogurts (FY) at 0.5–4.0% (w/w) to adsorb aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) was evaluated in vitro.

pmc-12492357.title: Environmental Lead Exposure Predicts Lower Bone Mineral Density in a Large Taiwanese Population-Based Study
pmc-12492357.creator: Po-Yin Shen, Fu-Wen Liang, Cheng-Chang Lu, Shu-Pin Huang, Szu-Chia Chen, Jiun-Hung Geng
pmc-12492357.description: Background: Chronic exposure to environmental lead (Pb) may impair bone metabolism and increase the risk of osteoporosis; however, large-scale epidemiological data remain limited. This study aimed to examine the association between long-term environmental Pb exposure and bone mineral density (BMD) in a nationally representative Taiwanese cohort.

pmc-12567332.title: Hydrogel-Based Finger Foods: Enhancing Nutritional Intake and Swallowing Safety in Older Persons with Dysphagia
pmc-12567332.creator: Enrika Lazickaitė, Milda Keršienė, Viktorija Eisinaitė, Ina Jasutienė, Gytė Damulevičienė, Daiva Leskauskaitė, Cristiano Capurso
pmc-12567332.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: Dysphagia is a common problem in older adults, characterized as a swallowing disorder that prevents food from passing from the mouth to the esophagus. Besides impairing dietary intake and leading to malnutrition, dysphagia also severely restricts water intake. Purpose: This study aimed to develop polysaccharide-based hydrogels as dysphagia-friendly finger foods designed to provide high water content and enable controlled vitamin delivery to older persons with dysphagia.

pmc-12619237.title: Mobile health and postoperative self-care following glaucoma, cataract, or corneal transplant surgeries
pmc-12619237.creator: Hamid Moghaddasi, Reza Rabiei, Hossein Valizadeh Laktarashi
pmc-12619237.description: BackgroundPostoperative self-care is a critical determinant of treatment outcomes in ophthalmic patients. Recent advances in mobile health (mHealth) and the widespread adoption of smartphones have created new opportunities to enhance disease management and promote self-care.ObjectiveThis study aimed to design and evaluate a mobile health application to support self-care among patients following glaucoma surgery, cataract extraction, and corneal transplantation.

pmc-13008706.title: Analysis of influencing factors and prediction of falls among rural older adults in China based on a nomogram model
pmc-13008706.creator: Yan Wu, Shangci Cao, Pengcheng Wan, Yuran Liu, Yaodong Zhao, Yujie Chen, Yi Li, Hong Ding
pmc-13008706.description: ObjectiveTo explore rural fall determinants and build a nomogram for high-risk identification. This study aims to preliminarily identify high-risk individuals and provide reference for subsequent intervention research.MethodsStratified multistage cluster sampling was used: one city from each of the northern, central, and southern regions of Anhui Province, one county per city, and six villages per county (18 villages total).

pmc-13105647.title: The next frontier of immunotherapy: clinical trial prospects for lung cancer vaccines
pmc-13105647.creator: Qing-Dong Zhu, Chang Song, Chun-Yan Zhao, Chang-Yue Jiang, Hang-Biao Qiang, Xiao-Mei Yang, Yi-Bo Lu, Zhou-Hua Xie
pmc-13105647.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Since William Coley’s pioneering work in the early 20th century, cancer vaccines have undergone more than a century of development, emerging as one of the most promising directions in oncology research and clinical translation[2]. This article systematically presents a comprehensive analysis of global clinical trial data on lung cancer vaccines, highlighting trends in development, trial design characteristics, and clinical outcomes, thereby providing a scientific foundation for the future optimization of lung cancer immunotherapy.
